#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Top-level run entry point. Orchestration details live in workflows/run_pipeline.py.
set -u

ROOT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)" || exit 2
PYTHON="$ROOT_DIR/.venv/bin/python"
if [ ! -x "$PYTHON" ]; then
  PYTHON="$(command -v python3 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ]; then
  echo "run.sh: Python 3 is required (activate .venv or install system python3)" >&2
  exit 2
fi
exec "$PYTHON" "$ROOT_DIR/workflows/run_pipeline.py" "$@"

decision.reason: This is a fresh, highly relevant CAD item: an independent engineering publication tested Backflip’s new drawing-, photo-, and video-to-CAD modalities on September 30. The strongest claims were checked rather than merely viewed: the reviewer imported downloaded STEP files into Fusion, applied 1060 aluminum, and found two TooTallToby drawing conversions exactly matched the target mass; it also documents a multibody failure and incomplete feature-tree imports. The photo and video results support only visual and limited dimensional observations, while Backflip CEO claims about inferred dimensions and expanding CAD access remain attributed commercial claims requiring broader, disclosed testing.
